def _narrow(path: str, mode: int) -> bool:
    """*path*'s mode narrowed to within *mode*; whether it is now - a file
    system without permissions takes the change and keeps the old mode."""
    now = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(path).st_mode)
    if now & ~mode:
        os.chmod(path, now & mode)
        now = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(path).st_mode)
    return not now & ~mode

class _RedactFilter(logging.Filter):
    """The safety net: every record masked, whether or not the call site
    remembered to - the addresses in it (an ffmpeg or mpv line quoting a
    stream's address with its token or login, redact_text) and the
    registered values, in its message, its arguments and the traceback it
    carries (exc_info). It fails closed: what could not be masked - a
    message whose arguments do not fit it, a value whose str() raises, a
    fault in the masking itself - is never written as it was, only a line
    that says one was withheld (WITHHELD), with the logger and the level
    still there; the record is kept, so a log still shows that something
    happened."""

    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        try:
            if record.args:
                # Formatted first, then masked whole: an address can be
                # split between the message and an argument, and masking
                # the message alone could eat a %s an argument needs.
                text = record.getMessage()
                record.msg, record.args = _escaped(redact_text(text)), ()
            else:
                msg = _redact_arg(record.msg)
                if not isinstance(msg, str):
                    text = str(msg)
                    msg = msg if _escaped(text) == text else text
                record.msg = _escaped(msg) if isinstance(msg, str) else msg
        except Exception as e:
            record.msg, record.args = f"{WITHHELD} ({type(e).__name__})", ()
        try:
            # Formatted here, once, masked: every handler's formatter uses
            # exc_text when it is there instead of formatting it again.
            if record.exc_info and not record.exc_text:
                record.exc_text = logging.Formatter().formatException(record.exc_info)
            if record.exc_text:
                record.exc_text = _escaped(redact_text(record.exc_text))
            if record.stack_info:
                record.stack_info = _escaped(redact_text(record.stack_info))
        except Exception as e:
            # Never the traceback as it was: a handler would format exc_info
            # again, unmasked.
            record.exc_info = None
            record.exc_text = f"{WITHHELD} - its traceback ({type(e).__name__})"
            record.stack_info = None
        return True

ACCEPTED_KEY = "settings_open_accepted"

def _tell_settings_not_private(self) -> None:
        """Once a start, when a settings file could not be made readable by
        this user alone (core/settings_files.py: a drive that keeps no
        permissions): asked in a window that waits for an answer - it holds
        every login - until the person says to go on for that file; after
        that a calm message each start. Its button opens the folder."""
        try:
            from ..core import settings_files
            found = settings_files.not_private()
            if not found or getattr(self, "_settings_open_told", False):
                return
            self._settings_open_told = True
            path = found[0]
            folder = os.path.dirname(path)

            def show() -> None:
                from ..core import xdg
                xdg.open_folder(folder)
            accepted = str(self.settings.value(settings_files.ACCEPTED_KEY, "") or "")
            if accepted != settings_files.accepted_mark(path):
                answer = self._ask_settings_open(path)
                if answer == "go":
                    self.settings.setValue(settings_files.ACCEPTED_KEY,
                                           settings_files.accepted_mark(path))
                    log.warning("settings: kept on a drive other accounts may read, as the "
                                "person said")
                    return
                if answer == "open":
                    show()
                log.warning("settings: the app closes - its settings file is not private")
                self.close()
                return
            hub_of(self).post(tr("settings_open_body", path=path), title=tr("settings_open_title"),
                              level="warning", action=show, action_label=tr("btn_open_folder"),
                              key="settings_not_private")
        except Exception as e:      # never in the way of starting
            log.warning("settings: the note on their permissions was not shown: %s", e)

    def _ask_settings_open(self, path: str) -> str:
        """The question a settings file others may read asks: "go" (go on
        with it, for this file), "open" (its folder, and close) or "quit" -
        Close the default, and Escape."""
        box = QMessageBox(QMessageBox.Icon.Warning, tr("settings_open_title"),
                          plain_text(tr("settings_open_body", path=path)),
                          QMessageBox.StandardButton.NoButton, self)
        opened = box.addButton(tr("btn_open_folder"), QMessageBox.ButtonRole.ActionRole)
        quit_btn = box.addButton(tr("settings_open_quit"), QMessageBox.ButtonRole.RejectRole)
        go = box.addButton(tr("settings_open_go"), QMessageBox.ButtonRole.AcceptRole)
        box.setDefaultButton(quit_btn)
        box.setEscapeButton(quit_btn)
        box.exec()
        clicked = box.clickedButton()
        return "go" if clicked is go else "open" if clicked is opened else "quit"

def fetch_details(self, title: str, kind: str,
                      year: int | None = None) -> dict | None:
        """Search by title (optionally narrowed by year), then fetch
        poster/rating/IMDb id/cast in one combined request
        (append_to_response) for the best match."""
        endpoint = "movie" if kind == "vod" else "tv"
        params: dict[str, Any] = {"api_key": self.api_key, "query": title,
                                  "include_adult": "false"}
        if year is not None:
            params["year" if endpoint == "movie"
                   else "first_air_date_year"] = year
        r = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE}/search/{endpoint}", params=params, timeout=10)
        r.raise_for_status()
        results = r.json().get("results") or []
        # If a year filter returned nothing, retry without it - the
        # provider's year can be wrong/missing and a title-only hit
        # still beats no cover.
        if not results and year is not None:
            params.pop("year", None)
            params.pop("first_air_date_year", None)
            r = requests.get(
                f"{self.BASE}/search/{endpoint}", params=params, timeout=10)
            r.raise_for_status()
            results = r.json().get("results") or []
        best = self._pick_result(results, year)
        if not best:
            return None
        tid = best.get("id")
        if tid is None:
            return None
        r2 = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE}/{endpoint}/{tid}",
            params={"api_key": self.api_key,
                    "append_to_response": "external_ids,credits"},
            timeout=10)
        r2.raise_for_status()
        d = r2.json()
        poster_path = d.get("poster_path") or best.get("poster_path")
        cast = []
        for c in (d.get("credits") or {}).get("cast") or []:
            name = c.get("name")
            if not name:
                continue
            profile_path = c.get("profile_path")
            cast.append({
                "name": name,
                "person_id": c.get("id"),
                "profile_url": (f"{self.PROFILE_IMG_BASE}{profile_path}"
                                if profile_path else None),
            })
            if len(cast) == 8:
                break
        genres = ", ".join(g.get("name", "") for g in d.get("genres") or []
                          if g.get("name"))
        release = (d.get("release_date") or d.get("first_air_date") or "")
        backdrop = d.get("backdrop_path") or best.get("backdrop_path")
        return {
            "tmdb_id": tid,
            "title": d.get("title") or d.get("name") or "",
            "poster_url": f"{self.IMG_BASE}{poster_path}" if poster_path else None,
            "backdrop_url": (f"{self.BACKDROP_IMG_BASE}{backdrop}"
                             if backdrop else None),
            "rating": d.get("vote_average") or None,
            "imdb_id": (d.get("external_ids") or {}).get("imdb_id"),
            "cast": cast,
            "overview": d.get("overview") or "",
            "genres": genres,
            "release_date": release,
        }

def bundled_tmdb_key() -> str:
    """The built-in TMDB key that makes posters work out of the box, so a
    user never has to create their own account.

    Read from the DOPEIPTV_TMDB_KEY environment variable (set for local
    dev and baked into release builds from a CI secret) or, failing that,
    an optional git-ignored ``dopeiptv/_tmdb_key.py`` exposing
    ``TMDB_API_KEY``. Deliberately NOT committed to the public repo, so
    the source tree carries no scrapeable secret while released binaries
    still ship a working key. A user's own key (Settings) always wins
    over this."""
    key = (os.environ.get("DOPEIPTV_TMDB_KEY") or "").strip()
    if key:
        return key
    try:
        from .._tmdb_key import TMDB_API_KEY  # type: ignore
        return (TMDB_API_KEY or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""

@staticmethod
    def clean_title(raw: str) -> tuple[str, int | None]:
        """Strip the noise providers wrap around real movie titles so
        the initial TMDB search stands a chance of matching. Handles
        leading language tags (EN|, SV -), quality/codec/audio tags
        (1080p, x265, WEB-DL, MULTI), and the bracketed suffixes
        Xtream operators add for indexing purposes ([IMDB], [MULTI],
        [SUB], plus empty [] or (something) that follow). Returns
        the cleaned title and the year if one appears in the raw
        string, so callers can pre-fill both a search box and a year
        filter. Shared between the auto-matcher (so covers show up
        for provider titles that TMDB would otherwise reject) and
        the manual-match dialog (so the search box lands on a sane
        starting query)."""
        t = raw or ""
        # Extract the year first, from the raw string, so a bracketed
        # or parenthesised year isn't collateral-damage of the
        # bracket-suffix strip a couple of lines down.
        year: int | None = None
        year_m = re.search(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", t)
        if year_m:
            try:
                year = int(year_m.group(0))
            except ValueError:
                year = None
        # Leading 'EN|', 'SV - ', 'FR:' language tag
        t = re.sub(r"^\s*[A-Za-z]{2,3}\s*[|\-:]\s*", "", t)
        # Remove EVERY bracketed segment anywhere in the title, not just
        # a single trailing one: '[AR-ENG]', '[MULTI]', '(1080p)',
        # '{x}'. Provider libraries often stack several, sometimes with
        # a dangling unclosed bracket ('... [AR-ENG] [').
        t = without_brackets(t)
        # Drop any leftover stray/unclosed bracket characters so a title
        # ending '... [' doesn't defeat the TMDB search.
        t = re.sub(r"[\[\](){}]", " ", t)
        # Codec / audio / language noise tail
        t = re.sub(
            r"\b(1080p|720p|2160p|4K|UHD|HDR|WEB[-.]?DL|WEB[-.]?RIP|"
            r"BR[-.]?RIP|BluRay|BDR[iI][pP]|x265|x264|HEVC|H\.?264|"
            r"H\.?265|AAC|DTS|AC3|MULTI|VOSTFR|VOST|VF|SUB|DUAL|"
            r"REMUX|EXTENDED|UNRATED|DIRECTORS?[ .]CUT)\b.*$", "",
            t, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        # Strip any leftover bare year, optionally in parens, so it
        # doesn't confuse the TMDB search string. The spaces before it
        # are taken whole from where they begin (_YEAR_LEFT): linear on a
        # long run of them.
        t = _YEAR_LEFT.sub(" ", t)
        # Trim leftover punctuation / whitespace
        t = t.strip(" -_.|:;/[](){}\t\n")
        t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t)
        return t, year

    def _ensure_fetch(self, title: str, kind: str, key: str) -> None:
        if key in self._pending:
            return
        self._pending.add(key)
        # Provider titles carry marketing noise (language prefix,
        # quality tags, '[IMDB]' / '[MULTI]' bracket suffixes, year
        # in parens) that TMDB's search endpoint scores against the
        # real title and rejects. Clean before searching so the
        # auto-match hits the same titles the manual dialog already
        # succeeds on.
        cleaned, year = self.clean_title(title)
        search_query = cleaned or title

        def fetch(t=search_query, k=kind, y=year):
            return self.client.fetch_details(t, k, y)

        def done(details, key=key, raw=title, q=search_query):
            # Never overwrite a manual pick with an auto-search result. This
            # can happen if the cache entry gets evicted and re-fetched.
            existing = self._cache.get(key) or {}
            if existing.get("manual"):
                self._pending.discard(key)
                self._on_resolved(key)
                return
            if details:
                _tmdb_dbg(f"MATCH  q={q!r} raw={raw!r} "
                          f"poster={bool(details.get('poster_url'))}")
            else:
                _tmdb_dbg(f"NOMATCH q={q!r} raw={raw!r}")
            self._cache[key] = details or {}
            self._failed.discard(key)
            self._save()
            self._pending.discard(key)
            self._on_resolved(key)

        def fail(msg, key=key, raw=title, q=search_query):
            # A TMDB request that timed out / hit a 5xx counts as
            # resolved-with-no-match: the delegate can safely fall
            # back to the provider cover from now on and stop
            # painting the placeholder letter. Notify waiting
            # callbacks the same way done() does so the row actually
            # gets a repaint instead of freezing on the placeholder.
            _tmdb_dbg(f"ERROR  q={q!r} raw={raw!r} {str(msg)[:80]}")
            self._failed.add(key)
            self._pending.discard(key)
            self._on_resolved(key)

        run_async(self.pool, fetch, done, fail)

_IPV4 = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?![\d.])")
# IPv6 in full (six groups or more, so a time like 21:05:03 is left alone)
# or shortened with "::" (fe80::1, ::1, 2001:db8:: and fe80:: too), an IPv4
# at its end with it (::ffff:192.0.2.7). "::" alone names nothing.
_IPV6 = re.compile(r"(?<![\w:])(?:(?:(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}:){5,7}[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}"
                   r"|[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}::[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}[0-9A-Fa-f])(?:(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})?"
                   r"|[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}[0-9A-Fa-f]::)(?![\w:])")
_MAC = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9A-Fa-f])(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}[:-]){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?![0-9A-Fa-f])")
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]{1,64}@[\w-]{1,63}(?:\.[\w-]{1,63})+")
# A supporter key pasted into a report would be the one thing that could tie it to a payment.
_SUPPORTER = re.compile(r"(?i)\bDS1-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}")
# A login written name=value or name: value - a quoted name or value too, as
# JSON and config files write them ("password": "x y"); the quotes stay.
# (The log's filter masks the same, core/log.py, all but the login and host.)
_KEYVAL = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(user(?:name)?|pass(?:word)?|pwd|(?:access_|refresh_|play_)?token|key|"
                     r"api[_-]?key|secret|auth|sid|session|mac|login|host)([\"']?\s*[=:]\s*)"
                     r"(\"[^\"\n]{0,200}\"|'[^'\n]{0,200}'|[^\s&'\",;]+)")
# A header that carries a login, to the end of its line, and a bearer token
# wherever it stands.
_AUTH_LINE = re.compile(r"(?i)\b((?:proxy-)?authorization|(?:set-)?cookie)([\"']?\s*[:=]\s*)[^\r\n]*")
_BEARER = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(bearer)\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}")
# A server written without its scheme ("iptv.example.com/live/..."): a name
# with a dot and a top-level domain, then a path. Not a file's path (one
# after a slash or a dot is part of it) and not a version (no letters).
_HOST_PATH = re.compile(r"(?<![\w@/.:-])(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,24}"
                        r"(?::\d{1,5})?/[^\s'\"<>()\[\]]*", re.IGNORECASE)


# A login told in words: "my password is hunter2", "lösenord: x",
# "username kalle" - the word after the name, in the languages most reports
# come in. ("login" and "pin" are left: "login failed", "the PIN was wrong".)
_SAID = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(password|passwd|passcode|username|user name|"
                   r"l\u00f6senord|anv\u00e4ndarnamn|passwort|benutzername|kennwort|"
                   r"mot de passe|identifiant|contrase\u00f1a|usuario|senha|usu\u00e1rio|"
                   r"wachtwoord|gebruikersnaam|has\u0142o|parola|salasana|adgangskode|passord)"
                   r"(\s*[:=]\s*|\s+(?:is now|is|was|\u00e4r|var|ist|est|es|\u00e9)?\s*)"
                   r"(?![\"']?<)([^\s,;.!?]{2,128})")
# A token whatever it is called: a JSON web token, a GitHub or Slack token,
# and any run of 32 or more letters and digits with both in it (a key, a
# hash that would name a file).
_JWT = re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}")
_PREFIXED = re.compile(r"\b(?:gh[pousr]|xox[abprs]|sk|pk|rk)[-_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}")
_LONG = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_/-])(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\d)(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]*[A-Za-z])"
                   r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])")
# Another account's home folder (Windows, macOS, Linux): its name.
_HOME_DIR = re.compile(r"(?i)((?:[A-Z]:)?[\\/](?:Users|home|Documents and Settings)[\\/])"
                       r"([^\\/\s:*?\"<>|]{1,64})")
# A phone number written as one usually is: with a + or 00 first.
_PHONE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w+])(?:\+|00)\d{1,3}(?:[ .-]?\d){6,13}(?!\d)")


def _hide_value(m: re.Match[str]) -> str:
    value = m.group(3)
    quote = value[0] if value[:1] in ("'", '"') else ""
    return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}{quote}<hidden>{quote}"


def _not_an_address(text: str) -> bool:
    """Loopback - or exactly this build's own version where it has four
    numbers ("1.6.8.259": a test build's run). Nothing else that only
    begins as the version does: 1.6.8.10 can be someone's address."""
    from .. import __version__
    return text.startswith("127.") or (text == __version__ and text.count(".") == 3)


def scrub(text: str, personal: Iterable[str] = ()) -> str:
    """*text* without anything that identifies a stream or a person."""
    # Whole addresses first (a login or a name inside one goes with it),
    # then the person's own values, longest first (a name inside another).
    out = _URL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}://<address>", text or "")
    for value in sorted({v.strip() for v in personal if v and len(v.strip()) >= 3}, key=len, reverse=True):
        out = re.sub(re.escape(value), "<private>", out, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    out = _SUPPORTER.sub("<supporter key>", out)
    out = _EMAIL.sub("<email>", out)
    out = _HOST_PATH.sub("<address>", out)
    out = _MAC.sub("<mac>", out)
    out = _IPV6.sub("<ip>", out)
    out = _IPV4.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if _not_an_address(m.group(0)) else "<ip>", out)
    out = _AUTH_LINE.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}<hidden>", out)
    out = _BEARER.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)} <hidden>", out)
    out = _KEYVAL.sub(_hide_value, out)
    out = _SAID.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}<hidden>", out)
    out = _JWT.sub("<token>", out)
    out = _PREFIXED.sub("<token>", out)
    out = _LONG.sub("<token>", out)
    out = _PHONE.sub("<phone>", out)
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    if len(home) > 1:
        out = out.replace(home, "~")
    out = _HOME_DIR.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}<user>", out)
    try:
        user = getpass.getuser()
    except Exception:
        user = ""
    if user and len(user) >= 3:
        out = re.sub(rf"(?<![\w]){re.escape(user)}(?![\w])", "<user>", out)
    return out


def personal_values(playlists: Iterable[dict], channels: Iterable[str] = (),
                    titles: Iterable[str] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """What the app knows to be someone's: sources' names, servers, logins
    and boxes; channel names; titles watched."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for p in playlists or []:
        for key in ("name", "server", "username", "password", "mac", "epg_url"):
            v = str(p.get(key) or "")
            if v:
                out.append(v)
                if key == "server":
                    host = re.sub(r"^[a-z]+://", "", v).split("/")[0].split("@")[-1].split(":")[0]
                    out.append(host)
    out += [str(c) for c in channels if c]
    out += [str(t) for t in titles if t]
    return out

def _over_https(url: str) -> str:
    """*url* if it is https - or this computer, for the tests' own servers;
    anything else is refused before a connection is made."""
    if build_check.secure(url):
        return url
    raise ValueError("reports go over https only")


def _post(url: str, body: bytes, timeout: float) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    """POST JSON with requests, whose certificates (certifi) travel with the
    app: urllib asks the system's OpenSSL for them, and a bundled Python on
    macOS has none, so every report failed there. Over https only, and to
    that address only: a redirect is not followed."""
    from .. import __version__
    from ._lazy_requests import requests
    r = requests.post(_over_https(url), data=body, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=False, headers={
        "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
        "User-Agent": f"dopeIPTV/{__version__}", "X-Dopeiptv-Report": "1",
        **build_check.headers()})
    return r.status_code, r.content

def send_status(kind: str, text: str, *, personal: Iterable[str], timeout: float = 15.0,
                endpoint: str | None = None, extra: dict | None = None) -> int:
    """send(), with the site's answer: its HTTP status - 409 for a reply to
    an answer whose thread is closed - or 0 when nothing reached it (never
    from a modified build). *personal*: what is the person's own
    (personal_values()) - required, so no way out sends without it."""
    from .. import __version__
    if not build_check.allowed():
        log.info("report: not sent - not an official build")
        return 0
    extra = extra or {}
    fields = {"kind": kind if kind in ("error", "crash", "feedback") else "feedback",
              "version": __version__, "os": platform.system(),
              # Scrubbed again here, whoever called, with the patterns and
              # what is the person's own: the last pass, so no way out
              # skips either.
              "text": scrub(text or "", personal)[:MAX_TEXT]}
    # What feedback is about (a topic, an area, how often) and "supporter":
    # "yes" from a supporter (read first): single words from a short list.
    fields.update({k: v for k, v in extra.items()

    for key in ("reply", "thread"):

    body = json.dumps(fields, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

        return status
    log.info("report: sent (%s%s)", kind, ", a reply" if "thread" in fields else "")

def _hide_value(m: re.Match) -> str:
    value = m.group(3)
    quote = value[0] if value[:1] in ("'", '"') else ""
    return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}{quote}<hidden>{quote}"


def scrub(text: str) -> str:
    out = _URL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}://<address>", text or "")
    out = _HOME.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}<user>", out)
    out = _SUPPORTER.sub("<supporter key>", out)
    out = _EMAIL.sub("<email>", out)
    out = _HOST_PATH.sub("<address>", out)
    out = _MAC.sub("<mac>", out)
    out = _IPV6.sub("<ip>", out)
    out = _IPV4.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if m.group(0).startswith("127.") else "<ip>", out)
    out = _AUTH_LINE.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}<hidden>", out)
    out = _BEARER.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)} <hidden>", out)
    return _KEYVAL.sub(_hide_value, out)

def _forget_quiet(now: float) -> int:
    """The addresses whose last request is older than their limit's window,
    forgotten: an address is held only as long as its limit needs it - ten
    minutes, a day for the daily ones - and a minute more at the most.
    Under _LOCK. How many went."""
    _SWEPT[0] = now
    gone = [k for k, v in _SEEN.items() if not v or now - v[-1] > _SPAN.get(k, WINDOW)]
    for key in gone:
        _SEEN.pop(key, None)
        _SPAN.pop(key, None)
    return len(gone)


def _forget_loop() -> None:
    """Every FORGET_EVERY: the quiet addresses forgotten, requests or none -
    the limits' here, and the failed sign-in tries' (admin_auth)."""
    while True:
        time.sleep(FORGET_EVERY)
        with _LOCK:
            _forget_quiet(time.monotonic())
        try:
            import admin_auth
            admin_auth.forget()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - the loop keeps its minute
            _fault(e, "forgetting")


def _allowed(addr: str, most: int = PER_WINDOW, window: float = WINDOW) -> bool:
    now = time.monotonic()
    with _LOCK:
        hits = [t for t in _SEEN.get(addr, []) if now - t < window]
        if window != WINDOW:
            _SPAN[addr] = window
        if len(hits) >= most:
            _SEEN[addr] = hits
            return False
        hits.append(now)
        _SEEN[addr] = hits
        if len(_SEEN) > 5000 or now - _SWEPT[0] >= FORGET_EVERY:
            _forget_quiet(now)
        return True

_SIGMA = (0x61707865, 0x3320646E, 0x79622D32, 0x6B206574)
_LANES = 256
#: 1 in the lowest bit of every lane, and each lane's own number in it.
_ONES = sum(1 << (64 * i) for i in range(_LANES))
_IOTA = sum(i << (64 * i) for i in range(_LANES))

_CLAMP = 0x0FFFFFFC0FFFFFFC0FFFFFFC0FFFFFFF


def _quarter(x: list[int], ia: int, ib: int, ic: int, id_: int,
             mask: int) -> None:
    """The quarter round (2.1) on four words of every lane at once. A
    rotation is a shift each way, one OR and one mask: what one lane shifts
    out lands above bit 31 of its own lane or the one below, and the mask
    drops it."""
    a, b, c, d = x[ia], x[ib], x[ic], x[id_]
    a = (a + b) & mask
    d ^= a
    d = ((d << 16) | (d >> 16)) & mask
    c = (c + d) & mask
    b ^= c
    b = ((b << 12) | (b >> 20)) & mask
    a = (a + b) & mask
    d ^= a
    d = ((d << 8) | (d >> 24)) & mask
    c = (c + d) & mask
    b ^= c
    b = ((b << 7) | (b >> 25)) & mask
    x[ia], x[ib], x[ic], x[id_] = a, b, c, d


def _keystream(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, counter: int, blocks: int) -> bytes:
    """*blocks* blocks of ChaCha20's key stream from block *counter* on."""
    if len(key) != 32 or len(nonce) != 12:
        raise ValueError("ChaCha20 takes a 32-byte key and a 12-byte nonce")
    if counter < 0 or counter + blocks > 1 << 32:
        raise ValueError("ChaCha20's block counter would wrap")
    k = struct.unpack("<8I", key)
    n = struct.unpack("<3I", nonce)
    out = bytearray(64 * blocks)
    done = 0
    while done < blocks:
        lanes = min(_LANES, blocks - done)
        ones = _ONES & ((1 << (64 * lanes)) - 1)
        mask = ones * _M32
        start = ((counter + done) * ones) + (_IOTA & ((1 << (64 * lanes)) - 1))
        init = [c * ones for c in _SIGMA] + [w * ones for w in k] \
            + [start] + [w * ones for w in n]
        x = list(init)
        for _ in range(10):
            _quarter(x, 0, 4, 8, 12, mask)      # columns
            _quarter(x, 1, 5, 9, 13, mask)
            _quarter(x, 2, 6, 10, 14, mask)
            _quarter(x, 3, 7, 11, 15, mask)
            _quarter(x, 0, 5, 10, 15, mask)     # diagonals
            _quarter(x, 1, 6, 11, 12, mask)
            _quarter(x, 2, 7, 8, 13, mask)
            _quarter(x, 3, 4, 9, 14, mask)
        base = 64 * done
        span = 64 * lanes
        for w in range(16):
            # Lane i of word w is block i's word w: 4 bytes at 64*i + 4*w.
            raw = ((x[w] + init[w]) & mask).to_bytes(8 * lanes, "little")
            for j in range(4):
                out[base + 4 * w + j:base + span:64] = raw[j::8]
        done += lanes
    return bytes(out)


def chacha20(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, counter: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    """*data* XOR the key stream from block *counter* (encrypt = decrypt)."""
    if not data:
        return b""
    stream = _keystream(key, nonce, counter, (len(data) + 63) // 64)
    n = len(data)
    return (int.from_bytes(data, "little")
            ^ int.from_bytes(stream[:n], "little")).to_bytes(n, "little")


def block(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, counter: int) -> bytes:
    """One 64-byte block of the key stream (RFC 8439, 2.3)."""
    return _keystream(key, nonce, counter, 1)


def poly1305(key: bytes, msg: bytes) -> bytes:
    """The 16-byte Poly1305 tag of *msg* under the one-time *key* (2.5)."""
    if len(key) != 32:
        raise ValueError("Poly1305 takes a 32-byte key")
    r = int.from_bytes(key[:16], "little") & _CLAMP
    s = int.from_bytes(key[16:], "little")
    acc = 0
    p = _P1305
    full = len(msg) - len(msg) % 16
    pad = 1 << 128
    for i in range(0, full, 16):
        acc = (acc + int.from_bytes(msg[i:i + 16], "little") + pad) * r % p
    if full < len(msg):
        rest = msg[full:]
        acc = (acc + int.from_bytes(rest, "little") + (1 << (8 * len(rest)))) * r % p
    return ((acc + s) & ((1 << 128) - 1)).to_bytes(16, "little")


def _pad16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\0" * (-n % 16)


def _tag(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, aad: bytes, ct: bytes) -> bytes:
    otk = block(key, nonce, 0)[:32]
    mac = b"".join((aad, _pad16(len(aad)), ct, _pad16(len(ct)),
                    struct.pack("<QQ", len(aad), len(ct))))
    return poly1305(otk, mac)


def encrypt(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, plaintext: bytes, aad: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    """The ciphertext with its 16-byte tag after it (2.8)."""
    ct = chacha20(key, nonce, 1, plaintext)
    return ct + _tag(key, nonce, aad, ct)


def decrypt(key: bytes, nonce: bytes, data: bytes, aad: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    """The plaintext; ValueError when the tag does not match (a changed
    byte, the wrong key or nonce or aad)."""
    if len(data) < 16:
        raise ValueError("too short for a Poly1305 tag")
    ct, tag = data[:-16], data[-16:]
    if not hmac.compare_digest(_tag(key, nonce, aad, ct), tag):
        raise ValueError("the data does not check out")
    return chacha20(key, nonce, 1, ct)

#: The copy's counter: one more on every upload, sealed with the rest, so
#: an earlier copy handed back is told from the latest. An entry in a
#: category of its own that no computer applies - an older app keeps it
#: as it keeps any entry (its merge takes the higher) without counting.
_META = "~"
_COUNTER = "n"


def counter(doc: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    e = (doc["c"].get(_META) or {}).get(_COUNTER)
    if not isinstance(e, dict) or not isinstance(e.get("v"), int):
        return 0
    return max(0, int(e["v"]))


def _counted(doc: dict[str, Any], n: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """*doc* with the counter *n* (its categories copied, so a shared one
    is not changed)."""
    out = _copy(doc)
    out["c"][_META] = dict(out["c"].get(_META) or {}, **{_COUNTER: {"t": n, "v": n}})
    return out

def round_trip(remote: Remote, key: bytes, doc: dict[str, Any], snap: Snapshot,
               cats: tuple[str, ...] | list[str], now: int | None = None,
               fresh: bool = False, joining: bool = False,
               seen: set[str] | frozenset[str] | None = None,
               bind: bool = False) -> RoundResult:
    """One sync, on a worker thread: the site's copy fetched, this
    computer's copy brought up to *snap* and merged in, and the result put
    back if it is any different - on a conflict (another computer was
    quicker) merged again with what it put there. *fresh*: joining; *seen*:
    the categories this computer has synced before (one it has not, that
    the site has already, starts fresh), and whether its shortcuts
    (newcomer()). *doc* itself is not changed. Each upload counts one more
    than the highest counter either side has (counter()); a copy whose
    counter is below the one *doc* has seen is older than what this
    computer had - the merge keeps this computer's newer entries anyway,
    and the result is put back and said (*older*). *bind*: this computer
    has not yet written the slot with its credential (auth_of) - put it
    back even unchanged, so the site binds the slot on this first round
    and from then on refuses anyone without the credential."""
    now = int(time.time()) if now is None else now
    highest = counter(doc)
    got = remote.get()
    if got is None and joining:
        raise SyncError("none")
    theirs = unseal(key, got[1]) if got else empty_doc()
    older = got is not None and counter(theirs) < highest
    if older:
        log.warning("sync: the copy there is older than one seen here (%d < %d) - "
                    "this computer's is put back", counter(theirs), highest)
    new_here: bool | set[str] = True if fresh else {
        c for c in cats if seen is not None and c not in seen and theirs["c"].get(c)}
    stamped = _copy(doc)
    stamp(stamped, snap, cats, now, new_here, newcomer(seen, theirs, snap.platform))
    for attempt in range(4):
        if attempt:
            # Another computer was quicker: its copy is the latest now.
            theirs = unseal(key, got[1]) if got else empty_doc()
            older = older or (got is not None and counter(theirs) < highest)
        version = got[0] if got else 0
        merged = merge(theirs, stamped)
        prune(merged, now)
        if got is not None and _canon(merged) == _canon(theirs) and not bind:
            return RoundResult(merged, stamped, version, False, len(got[1]), older)
        merged = _counted(merged, max(counter(merged), highest) + 1)
        blob = seal(key, merged)
        if len(blob) > MAX_BLOB:
            raise SyncError("big", len(blob))
        ok, info = remote.put(version, blob)
        if ok:
            return RoundResult(merged, stamped, int(info), True, len(blob), older)
        got = info
    raise SyncError("busy")

def open(self, url: str, key: str | None = None,
             source: str = "", private: bool = False) -> DvrSession:
        """The session for a channel about to be watched: its own again if
        it was watched before (or is being recorded), else a new one - the
        connection of source *source* (its id) from now. NotAStream for one
        whose provider sent a page or a message instead of a stream: this
        session it plays as it did before the buffer (mpv opens the address
        and says what it found). *private*: watched privately from its
        start - a new session's buffer in memory where there is room."""
        key = key or url
        with self._lock:
            s = self._sessions.get(key)
            if s is not None and s.closed:
                s = None
            if private and s is not None and not s.memory_cap \
                    and not s.recording and not s.held:
                # Its history of before is on the disk: what follows would
                # be written there too. Let go - in memory anew, or none.
                self._drop(s, "watched privately - not kept on the disk")

def signed_asset(release: dict, asset: dict) -> dict:
    """*asset* with the SHA-256 the release's signed checksum list gives
    it - the list signed with dopeIPTV's own key (core/update_keys.py).
    The site sends the list and its signature with the release
    (releases.json, nightly.json); otherwise they come from GitHub. With
    no signature, or one that is not by that key, or the file not on the
    list, the update stops: a site or mirror taken over cannot serve
    anything this accepts."""
    keys = []
    for k in UPDATE_KEYS:
        try:
            keys.append(base64.b64decode(k, validate=True))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    if not keys:
        # A build without the release key (core/update_keys.py) has nothing
        # to check a signature with: it takes no update at all rather than
        # trust a checksum the same site sent.
        log.error("update: this build carries no release key - no update is taken")
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_unsigned")
    tag = str(release.get("tag") or "")
    name = asset.get("name")
    if not names_version(str(name or ""), tag):
        # The signed list names files, not versions: a file of an older
        # release, still on its own signed list, offered under a newer tag
        # would pass refuse_older and the checksum both. Its name says its
        # version, and that name is what the list signs.
        log.error("update: %s is not a file of %s - not installed", name, tag or "(no version)")
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_unsigned")
    # The site's copy first; GitHub's when that one is missing, stale or
    # does not check out - the signature, not where it came from, decides.
    for where in ("site", "GitHub"):
        try:
            if where == "site":
                sums, sig = release.get("sums"), release.get("sums_sig")
                if not (sums and sig):
                    continue
            else:
                sums, sig = _github_file(tag, "SHA256SUMS"), _github_file(tag, "SHA256SUMS.sig")
            data = sums.encode() if isinstance(sums, str) else bytes(sums)
            raw_sig = base64.b64decode(sig.strip() if isinstance(sig, (str, bytes)) else b"",
                                       validate=True)
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("update: no signed checksum list for %s from %s: %s", tag, where, e)
            continue
        if not any(ed25519.verify(k, data, raw_sig) for k in keys):
            log.error("update: the checksum list of %s from %s is not signed with "
                      "dopeIPTV's key", tag, where)
            continue
        for line in data.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines():
            m = _SUMS_LINE.fullmatch(line.strip())
            if m and m.group(2) == name:
                return dict(asset, digest="sha256:" + m.group(1).lower())
        log.error("update: %s is not on the signed checksum list of %s from %s",
                  name, tag, where)
    raise UpdateError("upd_err_unsigned")


def _expected_sha256(asset: dict) -> str | None:
    digest = str(asset.get("digest") or "")
    m = re.fullmatch(r"sha256:([0-9a-fA-F]{64})", digest)
    return m.group(1).lower() if m else None


def download(asset: dict, dest: Path,
             progress: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
             cancel: threading.Event | None = None) -> None:
    """Fetch *asset* to *dest*, verifying size and digest. Removes a partial
    or mismatching file before raising."""
    size = int(asset.get("size") or 0)
    sha = _expected_sha256(asset)
    # Nothing is fetched that cannot be checked, or from an address that
    # is not https - nor from one a redirect leads to (_get_https).
    if not str(asset.get("url") or "").startswith("https://"):
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_not_https")
    if not sha:
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_no_checksum")
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    got = 0
    # A server that sends more than the file is stops being read there,
    # not once the disk is full: it cannot match the signed checksum. The
    # size a site says is never more than DOWNLOAD_MAX either.
    if size > DOWNLOAD_MAX:
        log.error("update: %s says it is %d bytes - more than any release file", asset.get("name"), size)
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_checksum")
    limit = size or DOWNLOAD_MAX
    try:
        with _get_https(asset["url"], stream=True, timeout=30) as r:
            r.raise_for_status()
            total = size or int(r.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            # A file of our own making, never one that was lying there: in a
            # folder others may write to, a file (or a link) put under this
            # name beforehand would be theirs to change after the checksum.
            dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            with open(dest, "xb") as fh:
                for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=1 << 16):
                    if cancel is not None and cancel.is_set():
                        raise UpdateError("cancelled")
                    if not chunk:
                        continue
                    got += len(chunk)
                    if got > limit:
                        log.error("update: %s sent more than its %d bytes - stopped",
                                  asset.get("name"), limit)
                        raise UpdateError("upd_err_checksum")
                    fh.write(chunk)
                    h.update(chunk)
                    if progress is not None:
                        progress(got, total)
        if size and got != size:
            raise UpdateError("upd_err_incomplete", got=got, size=size)
        if h.hexdigest() != sha:
            raise UpdateError("upd_err_checksum")
    except UpdateError:
        dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise UpdateError("upd_err_download", error=e) from e

def lan_address() -> str:
    """This machine's address on the LAN, as the Chromecast will see it.

    A UDP socket is 'connected' to an outside address to find out which
    interface the kernel would route through - nothing is sent, and it is the
    only way that survives a machine with several interfaces (Wi-Fi, Ethernet,
    a VPN, Docker) where the hostname resolves to the wrong one.
    """
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    try:
        s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80))
        return s.getsockname()[0]
    except Exception:
        return "127.0.0.1"
    finally:
        s.close()

    signed long ago stays signed, so a site taken over could hand out an
    old one, with the faults fixed since. Newer than this copy it must be -
    or, as on the Releases channel today, the release a test build carries
    the number of (1.4.0 over 1.4.0.12: updates.offered)."""

def _get_https(url: str, *, headers: Callable[[str], dict] = site_headers,
               get: Callable[..., Any] | None = None, **kw):
    """GET *url*, following its redirects by hand: each address https (a
    release's file on GitHub moves on to its storage, never to plain http),
    and each hop's headers its own (*headers* of its address) - the build's
    kind only to dopeiptv.org. A first address on this computer (a test's
    own server) may be http, and lead on to this computer alone. *get*:
    the requests.get to use (the caller's own)."""
    local = url.startswith("http://") and _loopback(url)
    for _ in range(_HOPS + 1):
        if not (url.startswith("https://") or (local and url.startswith("http://") and _loopback(url))):
            raise UpdateError("upd_err_not_https")
        r = (get or requests.get)(url, allow_redirects=False, headers=headers(url), **kw)
        if not getattr(r, "is_redirect", False):
            return r
        from urllib.parse import urljoin
        nxt = urljoin(url, r.headers.get("Location") or "")
        r.close()
        url = nxt
    raise UpdateError("upd_err_download", error="too many redirects")

    """A visitor, a download or an update as a mark: HMAC-SHA256 of *parts*
    with the key of *day*'s month (state["_keys"], in memory alone), cut to
    twelve characters. Never written down as it is: a visit kept carries a

    day, another on every other day - nothing kept ties two days together."""
    key = _keys(state, day).key(_month(day))

def seal(state: dict, day: str, vid: str) -> tuple:
    """The visitor's mark, sealed with its month's key for the visit kept:
    ("w", "e") - random to anyone without the key (a new nonce each time,
    so two visits of one visitor look nothing alike), the mark again to
    this service while the key is kept (unseal). "e" names the key."""
    keys = _keys(state, day)
    month = _month(day)
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{12}", vid or ""):

    nonce = secrets.token_bytes(6)
    pad = hmac.new(keys.key(month), b"w|" + nonce, hashlib.sha256).digest()[:6]
    body = bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(bytes.fromhex(vid), pad, strict=True))
    return (nonce + body).hex(), keys.kid(month)
